scope: Only CacheOPT, JITServe, and UniBoost main mechanisms relevant to recovery, headroom and protection. No new GPU run, implementation, or broader novelty search.

local_witness.native_action: Restore succeeds; consumes 8 blocks; same request re-preempted at call 116.
local_witness.runway_action: Defers at call 115; restores at call 161 and completes.
local_witness.information_contract: Known prompt plus already generated tokens, current APC credit and resident block boundaries; no future output length or EOS oracle, speculative completion release, persistent reservation, or guaranteed protected interval.
local_witness.limits: Observed counters, successful allocations, schedules and output prefixes agree before call 115; full block ownership and GPU state were not recorded. Subsequent policy trajectories differ.

methods.name: CacheOPT
methods.mechanism: Predicts padded output demand; embeds requests in allocated-but-unused capacity; orders waiting/preempted requests by remaining TTFT/TBT allowance. Critical demand can trigger eviction. Proactive allocation and a separately tracked shared reserve reduce allocation failures.
methods.overlap: Direct prior coverage of advance capacity provisioning and avoiding preemption. The printed policy is not the exact one-step physical sum.
methods.action_on_local_state: UNDETERMINED: free13/candidate8/resident-next46 omits its predicted demand, criticality, allocations and reserve. It may change the victim or request selection; do not assert admission versus deferral.
minimum_extra_state: Padded length estimates and confidence parameters
TTFT/TBT contracts, remaining allowances, critical sets, historical maximum iteration time
Per-request allocated/used capacity; embedding and expected release dependencies
Reserve inventory, allocation quantum, proactive horizon and victim order
methods.minimum_implementation: Selection, proactive/reserve allocator and eviction policy; map logical reservations to shared physical APC blocks without double credit. Resolve allocation-quantum units instead of equating the paper example with our eight blocks.

methods.name: JITServe
methods.mechanism: Schedules goodput per estimated serving bandwidth within frames. It models swap/recompute stalls and permits priority-driven preemption only when projected gain exceeds cost; frame boundaries suppress churn. Its backend inherits prefix caching.
methods.overlap: Direct prior treatment of recovery cost and stability. A scheduling frame is not, in these sections, a physical KV reservation guaranteeing residency throughout that frame.
methods.action_on_local_state: UNDETERMINED: the three block counts cannot identify its selected batch or gain-versus-cost decision. No explicit resident-next-block sum was found in these sections.
minimum_extra_state: Online remaining-length bounds, token-time estimates and aging
Frame duration/phase, service already granted, priority, cutoff and group size
Hardware-calibrated swap/recompute costs, candidate gain and selected batch
methods.minimum_implementation: Frame scheduler, online estimates, grouping and cost test, plus declared handling of forced allocator evictions. Preserve APC. A retrospective diagnostic latency threshold cannot substitute for an actual SLO contract.

methods.name: UniBoost / MemGuard
methods.mechanism: Quantizes attained work geometrically and protects dispatched requests until the next threshold. Algorithm 1 checks U+KVNeed(r,c)<=B for the next chunk/step; no explicit protected-window reservation formula appears. A.5 proposes cache-hit credit in effective work, not physical shared-block accounting.
methods.overlap: Strongest overlap: prediction-free stabilization and minimum useful service after dispatch. Our admission-only one-step gate is not a minimum-run guarantee.
methods.action_on_local_state: UNDETERMINED. Conditionally, the printed capacity check passes if this head is selected and KVNeed=8. This is not a full MemGuard action: priorities, protected victims and memory-pressure handling remain unresolved.
minimum_extra_state: Attained decode work, bin k, next threshold, dispatch/protection flags and recomputation semantics
Arrival/phase-entry, gamma, hysteresis, queue priorities, per-request KVNeed and eligible victims
methods.minimum_implementation: Priority/bin/protection state machine; define forced-memory eviction and no-eligible-victim behavior. A guaranteed window additionally needs physical growth-to-threshold, APC ownership and reservation/release accounting; that would be an adapter addition.
methods.version_limit: HTML and PDF v1 checked. PMLR entry confirmed; its PDF text was not verified. Missing-detail findings apply only to v1.

fair_comparison_contract: Run an implemented policy or an explicitly named component adapter under the same model, input, capacity, APC, block size, token budget and decode contract; do not reconstruct a policy verdict from missing state.

For each decision log physical free/reclaimable counts, shared-block/refcount ownership, current reservations, candidate identity, policy state, chosen action, successful allocations and later preemption/recovery.
Use only information available at the decision. Do not use final output lengths, future EOS or uncommitted future release as online inputs.
Separate priority-caused eviction from native allocator pressure, and failed native allocation from policy deferral.
Keep exact-action comparison conditional on a common observable prestate; use whole-policy comparisons after trajectories diverge.

conclusion.mechanism_novelty: Substantial prior coverage; one-step recovery gate alone is not supported as a new contribution.
conclusion.exact_action_equivalence: Not established for any of the three methods on this witness. Absence of an identical printed inequality does not establish novelty or a contrary baseline action.
conclusion.bounded_next_step: If comparing this mechanism, implement and label the nearest protection/reserve component with explicit missing-state choices before claiming benefit beyond those mechanisms.
